title: Ear, Mouth, Nose, and Heart at R4

lessons.title: Ear and mouth return at R4
lessons.gloss: retrieve ear and mouth with their unrelated lookalike and worn-consonant histories at R4

segments.text: Say kann and mūnh from memory: ear, mouth. Keep the two meanings separate before looking at the script.
Read ਕੰਨ, ਮੂੰਹ once. This lesson measures listening, speech, and recognition. It does not award independent Gurmukhi writing evidence.

segments.prompt: Say ear and mouth in Punjabi. Which word only sounds as though it belongs with karnā, to do?
acceptedResponses: kann / mūnh; kann is unrelated to karnā
kann / munh; kann is unrelated to karna
ਕੰਨ ਮੂੰਹ; ਕੰਨ is unrelated to ਕਰਨਾ

feedback.correct: Both meanings returned, and kann stayed separate from karnā.
feedback.incorrect: Repair one link at a time: kann is ear, mūnh is mouth, and kann is not related to karnā.

segments.prompt: Match the old histories: karṇa without any link to karnā; mukha whose kh weakened and disappeared into a level high tone.
acceptedResponses: kann — karṇa, unrelated to karnā; mūnh — mukha, with kh lost into level high tone
kann - karna ear root not do; munh - mukha lost kh high tone

feedback.correct: The false resemblance and the real sound change stayed distinct.
feedback.incorrect: Kann belongs with karṇa, ear, not karnā, do. Mūnh comes from mukha after kh weakened and disappeared.

segments.text: Say both meanings and one history for each, then stop. No new body word follows.

lessons.title: Nose and heart return at R4
lessons.gloss: retrieve nose and heart with their inherited and borrowed histories at R4

segments.text: Say nakk and dil from memory: nose, heart. Hold the doubled consonant in the first word.
Read ਨੱਕ, ਦਿਲ once. This lesson measures listening, speech, and recognition. It does not award independent Gurmukhi writing evidence.

segments.prompt: Say nose and heart in Punjabi, in that order.

feedback.correct: Nose and heart returned in the requested order.
feedback.incorrect: Repair only the missed link: nakk is nose; dil is heart.

segments.prompt: Which word is inherited and cognate with English nose, and which is a Persian loan with a deeper shared ancestor behind English heart?
acceptedResponses: nakk is the inherited nose cognate; dil is the persian heart loan
nakk inherited nose; dil persian heart

feedback.correct: The inherited nose word and borrowed heart word kept their different routes.
feedback.incorrect: Nakk is inherited and cognate with nose. Dil came through Persian, though it shares a deeper ancestor with heart.

segments.text: Say both meanings and contrast their routes once: inherited nakk, borrowed dil. Then stop.
